rules.name: Multi-Channel Financial Tracking

direction.title: Expand Financial Investigation to All Channels
direction.description: When direct financial evidence is absent, investigate banking records, UPI transaction trails, cryptocurrency wallets, hawala networks, and bullion dealers. Professional fraudsters often use layered financial obfuscation.
direction.trigger: Financial-fraud hypothesis is active; the visible financial evidence (if any) is only a fragment of the likely full trail.
cross_match: Timing of transfers against the incident timeline
direction.expected_outcome: Maps the full money trail across channels, revealing counterparties, off-ramps, and the scale of the operation.

rules.why_template: Financial fraud hypothesis is active — expanding to all financial channels is essential as perpetrators often use multiple obfuscation layers.

rules.name: Cryptocurrency Wallet Trail

direction.title: Trace Cryptocurrency Wallet & Off-Ramp
direction.description: A crypto wallet or QR code found in case evidence is a distinct, high-value lead in its own right. Walk the transaction graph from the wallet to its counterparties and identify where funds were converted back to cash (exchange, P2P off-ramp, or physical bullion).
direction.trigger: A crypto wallet address, QR code, or exchange reference appears anywhere in the case evidence.
cross_match: Off-ramp KYC identity against case suspects
direction.expected_outcome: Identifies the real-world identity behind the wallet at the point it touches a regulated exchange or KYC'd counterparty.

rules.why_template: A crypto wallet reference in the evidence is a self-contained investigation lead — it either resolves to a KYC'd identity or confirms the money never left the crypto ecosystem.
